content.title: About
content.content: Solid Monterey Jack cheese is made from cow's milk in California, USA. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor, a creamy texture, and a characteristic yellow hue. The cheese is aged from 2 to 6 months, giving it firmness and a subtle sharpness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is named after the city of Monterey, where production began in the early 20th century.
Monterey Jack is a staple in Mexican‑inspired dishes such as fajitas and nachos.
When aged in warmer conditions, the cheese may develop an orange tint from added annatto.
It melts easily, making it popular for casseroles and sauces.
In the United States, Monterey Jack is one of the most popular grilling cheeses.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides a high amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Delivers high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: During aging some lactose is broken down, making the cheese more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Includes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese is salted, so individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Solid cheese is calorie‑dense; portion control is important for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Contains saturated fat, which can affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Monterey Jack can be cubed, shredded, or sliced. It works well in sandwiches, burgers, casseroles, salads, and as a topping for tacos. Shredded cheese melts quickly, creating a flavorful crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in its original packaging or an airtight container at 1‑4 °C. For longer storage, freeze up to 3 months after cutting into portions. Before use, check for mold or off‑odors.
